summary:
Beyond the Mission is an educational space-exploration project about the hardware NASA has left across the solar system since the 1960s.
The main purpose is to make the history of space exploration easier and more exciting to learn. Information about old missions is often spread across technical websites and textbooks, which can be difficult for younger audiences. The challenge is to turn this information into engaging stories using creative ideas such as our website.
The website Beyond the Mission presents this idea through visual storytelling showcases two NASA missions - Opportunity and Voyager 1.
The machines left behind and those still travelling carry important stories about engineering, discovery and human curiosity. By presenting their histories and science in an accessible way, we intend to present the marvel of engineering and space exploration.
details:
‘Beyond the Mission’ is a web-based storytelling project created by Team CosmicMambazham to answer the challenge around using NASA’s space exploration equipment and explaining the science behind the discoveries. It aims to educate young students and space enthusiasts of some of the amazing robotic explorers we have sent into space.

The main concept behind our project is:

What happens when machines exceed their missions?

We have chosen two amazing NASA missions, Opportunity (Oppy) and Voyager 1 to explore, using storytelling and visual media to explain everything they have achieved on their missions. We have included details about the engineering, scientific equipment, achievements and milestones they have made.

What does the Project Do and How Does It Work?

Our project looks at two robotic missions which have gone above and beyond their expectations.

Opportunity (Oppy) is a Mars Exploration Rover launched by NASA on the 7th July 2003 and landed on Mars on the 25th January 2004. It was designed to last only 90 Sols, however, it has lasted for an incredible 5111 Sols. We have explained the engineering behind the Opportunity rover. This includes the solar panels, 6 wheel drive, robotic arm, Rock Abrasion Tool, camera and spectrographs. These have enabled the rover to explore the surface of Mars, analyse rocks and soil, uncover fresh rock and analyse geological features.We have also explained how these engineering features have helped us learn new scientific things. The rover has discovered evidence of water from long ago on Mars and geological features showing that some areas of Mars were once wet. The story of Opportunity ends with the huge dust storm in June 2018 which blocked the sun from shining onto their solar panels. NASA have declared the end of the mission on the 13th February 2019.

We explore Voyager 1 which was launched on the 5th September 1977 to explore the outer planets, moons, atmosphere and magnetosphere. This mission has many engineering features such as the high gain antenna, Radioisotope Thermoelectric Generators (RTG), camera, magnetometer boom and thruster. We have explained what each feature does and how they have helped the rover communicate with earth, provide electricity, record scientific data and keep it in the right position. The mission has discovered many things such as Io (a volcanic moon of Jupiter). It has also discovered the Great Red Spot on Jupiter, the complex ring structure of Saturn and what is like in interstellar space. The Voyager 1 has also entered interstellar space in 2012 and taken the famous Pale Blue Dot image in 1990. This image shows how small the Earth appears from 6 billion km away.

These missions have shown how engineering can help achieve scientific wonders.

Benefits and Impact

The main objective of this project was to make space science accessible and interesting to young students. Often science missions can be complicated and have lots of information to take in. This can be hard for younger students to understand.

However, by incorporating the information into a story it has helped us connect the information. We have explained how specific pieces of equipment have helped us achieve what we have on the missions. We explain what they do, why they are needed and what we have learnt from them.

There are many benefits to this project, these include:

Increased scientific knowledge – Informing people about key milestones in planetary exploration and science.

Increased appreciation of engineering – Explaining how pieces of equipment, scientific instruments and power sources on the spacecraft have come together to achieve great things.

Understanding concepts – Connects engineering concepts to scientific discoveries.

Increased historical knowledge – Tells the story of amazing robotic explorers.

Encouraging curiosity – Encourages young students to look into astronomy, robotics, physics and engineering.

The impact of this project is to teach people to appreciate the engineering achievements of NASA missions. This will also show them how machines designed on Earth can help us explore places we have never been to before.

In the future we hope to inspire the next generation of scientists, engineers and space enthusiasts.

Tools / Technology / Methodology

We chose to make this project a web-based one so more people can access it.

Our project is hosted on Vercel.

We have used a digital approach to this project. Including visual storytelling, well organised scientific information and telling a story. We have split our content into sections to show people how the missions have progressed. Telling them the objective, equipment, discoveries and milestones.

The technology used:

Web-based education project.

Hosting on Vercel.

Researching and finding information about NASA missions.

Visual storytelling.

Creativity and Innovation

The creativity of our project comes from the storytelling aspect.

Usually when people learn about space exploration they are given facts about when they were launched, what they were trying to achieve and what they have discovered. However, this doesn’t always show how challenging the engineering can be and doesn’t always create a connection with the audience.

We wanted to try a different approach.

Our story revolves around the robotic explorers going far beyond what we expected them to. Opportunity has gone way beyond what we expected. It was designed for a short mission however it has lasted over 10 years. Voyager 1 represents our ambition to explore beyond our solar system.

We also wanted to include two missions with very different engineering. Opportunity uses solar to power itself on Mars. Voyager 1 uses Radioisotope Thermoelectric Generators to provide electricity for it. This helps to show how engineering must change to suit the mission and environment. Including the Pale Blue Dot image has added a creative element. This has added an emotional and philosophical aspect to the scientific story. This will help people to appreciate how big space really is.

We have tried to create an educational experience by using engineering concepts, historical milestones, scientific discoveries and storytelling.

Considerations

When creating our project we considered:

Accuracy – We wanted to give accurate information about the timeline, objective, equipment and discoveries made. We wanted the information to be accurate to how much they actually achieved.

Accessibility – As we are targeting young students we wanted to make sure the information was easy to understand.

Storytelling – We have organised our content to explain how the missions have progressed from their original purpose, to the engineering, scientific achievements and how they have gone beyond what was expected.

Visual – We have thought about how we can present the information in a visually appealing way.

Educational – We have included all key pieces of equipment and milestones to show how they have contributed to space exploration.

Overall Vision

Ultimately our project is an attempt to tell the story of the amazing machines which have helped us explore beyond our limits. From Opportunity analysing the ancient geological history of Mars to Voyager 1 exploring interstellar space, these missions show how amazing science and engineering can be.

We want people to look past the machines and understand the knowledge, effort and creativity behind every piece of equipment, observation and km travelled. We want to bring these forgotten robotic explorers to life through stories to inspire the next generation of explorers.
